################################################################################
# FILE: tests/test_critique_fixes.py
################################################################################
"""Tests covering fixes for the 5 production critique issues:
1. Column-to-column comparison in filter() without silent footgun
2. map() boolean safety and mixed-type guard
3. DataFrame constructor with list-of-dicts
4. Unbracketed special-character column names (parentheses, etc.) in filter & mutate
5. Dynamic column resolution via col(@var) and col('name')
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import polars as pl
import pytest

import pytae as pt

# =============================================================================
# Issue 3: DataFrame Constructor with list of dicts
# =============================================================================


def test_dataframe_constructor_list_of_dicts():
    data = [{"a": 1, "b": 2}, {"a": 3, "b": 4}]
    df = pt.DataFrame(data)
    assert isinstance(df, pt.DataFrame)
    assert len(df) == 2
    assert list(df.columns) == ["a", "b"]
    assert list(df["a"]) == [1, 3]
    assert list(df["b"]) == [2, 4]


def test_dataframe_constructor_single_dict_in_list():
    df = pt([{"x": 10, "y": 20}])
    assert isinstance(df, pt.DataFrame)
    assert len(df) == 1
    assert list(df.columns) == ["x", "y"]
    assert df["x"][0] == 10


# =============================================================================
# Issue 1: Filter Column-to-Column Comparison & Typo Safety
# =============================================================================


def test_filter_column_to_column_equality():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "tranche_id": ["T1", "T2", "T3", "T4"],
            "deal_id": ["T1", "D2", "T3", "D4"],
        }
    )
    res = df.filter("tranche_id == deal_id")
    assert len(res) == 2
    assert list(res["tranche_id"]) == ["T1", "T3"]


def test_filter_column_to_column_inequality_and_ordering():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "amount": [100, 200, 300, 400],
            "limit": [150, 150, 350, 350],
        }
    )
    # Greater than
    gt = df.filter("amount > limit")
    assert len(gt) == 2
    assert list(gt["amount"]) == [200, 400]

    # Less than or equal
    lte = df.filter("amount <= limit")
    assert len(lte) == 2
    assert list(lte["amount"]) == [100, 300]

    # Not equal
    neq = df.filter("amount != limit")
    assert len(neq) == 4


def test_filter_unquoted_non_column_raises_keyerror():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"species": ["Adelie", "Gentoo", "Chinstrap"]})
    with pytest.raises(KeyError) as exc_info:
        df.filter("species == Gentoo")
    msg = str(exc_info.value)
    assert "column 'Gentoo' not found in DataFrame" in msg
    assert "quote it like 'Gentoo'" in msg


def test_filter_quoted_scalar_still_matches():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"species": ["Adelie", "Gentoo", "Chinstrap"]})
    res = df.filter("species == 'Gentoo'")
    assert len(res) == 1
    assert res["species"][0] == "Gentoo"


def test_filter_with_at_var_scalar():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"amount": [10, 50, 100, 200]})
    threshold = 50  # noqa: F841
    res = df.filter("amount > @threshold")
    assert len(res) == 2
    assert list(res["amount"]) == [100, 200]


def test_filter_with_at_var_column_via_col():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "tranche_id": ["T1", "T2", "T3"],
            "deal_id": ["T1", "X2", "T3"],
        }
    )
    target = "deal_id"  # noqa: F841
    res = df.filter("tranche_id == col(@target)")
    assert len(res) == 2
    assert list(res["tranche_id"]) == ["T1", "T3"]


# =============================================================================
# Issue 2: map() Boolean Safety & Mixed-Type Guards
# =============================================================================


def test_map_returns_boolean_series():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"code": ["2B", "3C", "4D"]})
    res = df.mutate("flag = map(code, {'2B': False, '3C': True}, default=False)")
    assert res["flag"].dtype == pl.Boolean
    assert list(res["flag"]) == [False, True, False]


def test_map_boolean_without_default_fills_nulls():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"code": ["2B", "3C", "4D"]})
    res = df.mutate("flag = map(code, {'2B': False, '3C': True})")
    assert res["flag"].dtype == pl.Boolean
    assert res["flag"][0] is False
    assert res["flag"][1] is True
    assert res["flag"][2] is None


def test_map_mixed_mapping_values_raises_typeerror():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"code": ["2B", "3C"]})
    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as exc_info:
        df.mutate("flag = map(code, {'2B': 'SC', '3C': False})")
    assert "cannot mix boolean and non-boolean" in str(exc_info.value)


def test_map_string_values_with_boolean_default_raises_typeerror():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"code": ["2B", "3C"]})
    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as exc_info:
        df.mutate("flag = map(code, {'2B': 'SC'}, default=False)")
    assert "cannot mix non-boolean mapping values with boolean default" in str(exc_info.value)


def test_map_boolean_values_with_string_default_raises_typeerror():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"code": ["2B", "3C"]})
    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as exc_info:
        df.mutate("flag = map(code, {'2B': False}, default='SC')")
    assert "cannot mix boolean mapping values with non-boolean default" in str(exc_info.value)


def test_map_normal_strings_and_numbers_preserved():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"code": ["2B", "3C", "9Z"]})
    res = df.mutate(
        "s_code = map(code, {'2B': 'Senior', '3C': 'Mezz'}, default='Junior')",
        "n_code = map(code, {'2B': 1, '3C': 2}, default=0)",
    )
    assert list(res["s_code"]) == ["Senior", "Mezz", "Junior"]
    assert list(res["n_code"]) == [1, 2, 0]


# =============================================================================
# Issue 4: Special Characters in Column Names
# =============================================================================


def test_special_column_names_in_mutate():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"irba_unsecured_lgd_(1g00)": [0.2, 0.7, 0.4]})
    res = df.mutate("scaled = irba_unsecured_lgd_(1g00) * 100")
    assert list(res["scaled"]) == [20.0, 70.0, 40.0]


def test_special_column_names_in_filter():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"irba_unsecured_lgd_(1g00)": [0.2, 0.7, 0.4]})
    res = df.filter("irba_unsecured_lgd_(1g00) > 0.5")
    assert len(res) == 1
    assert res["irba_unsecured_lgd_(1g00)"][0] == 0.7


def test_multiple_special_columns_in_complex_mutate():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "irba_unsecured_lgd_(1g00)": [0.2, 0.7, 0.4],
            "post_crm_lgd_(2a)": [0.1, 0.9, 0.3],
        }
    )
    res = df.mutate(
        "diff = irba_unsecured_lgd_(1g00) - post_crm_lgd_(2a)",
        "chosen = if_else(irba_unsecured_lgd_(1g00) > 0.5, post_crm_lgd_(2a), 0.0)",
    )
    assert len(res) == 3
    assert list(res["chosen"]) == [0.0, 0.9, 0.0]


# =============================================================================
# Issue 5: Dynamic Column Resolution via col(...)
# =============================================================================


def test_col_dynamic_variable_in_mutate():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"sales_2023": [10, 20], "sales_2024": [30, 40]})
    target = "sales_2024"  # noqa: F841
    res = df.mutate("growth = col(@target) * 1.1")
    assert [round(x, 1) for x in res["growth"]] == [33.0, 44.0]


def test_col_literal_string_in_mutate():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"sales": [100, 200]})
    res = df.mutate("out = col('sales') / 2")
    assert list(res["out"]) == [50.0, 100.0]


def test_col_bare_name_in_mutate():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"sales": [100, 200]})
    res = df.mutate("out = col(sales) / 2")
    assert list(res["out"]) == [50.0, 100.0]


def test_col_with_unknown_name_raises_keyerror_with_hint():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"revenue": [100, 200]})
    with pytest.raises(KeyError) as exc_info:
        df.mutate("out = col('revenu') * 2")
    msg = str(exc_info.value)
    assert "column 'revenu' not found in DataFrame" in msg
    assert "did you mean 'revenue'?" in msg


def test_special_column_names_with_null_predicates():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "counterparty_class_(irb)": ["Sovereign", None, "Corporate"],
            "counterparty class (irb)": ["Gov", "Bank", None],
        }
    )
    assert len(df.filter("counterparty_class_(irb).is_not_null()")) == 2
    assert len(df.filter("counterparty_class_(irb).is_null()")) == 1
    assert len(df.filter("[counterparty class (irb)].is_not_null()")) == 2
    assert len(df.filter("[counterparty class (irb)].is_null()")) == 1

    # SQL 'is null' syntax in filter raises explicit guidance
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc:
        df.filter("counterparty_class_(irb) is null")
    assert "use 'counterparty_class_(irb).is_null()'" in str(exc.value)

    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc2:
        df.filter("counterparty_class_(irb) is not null")
    assert "use 'counterparty_class_(irb).is_not_null()'" in str(exc2.value)


def test_map_empty_dict_with_boolean_default():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"post_crm_brr": ["A", "B", "C"]})
    res_false = df.mutate("flag = map(post_crm_brr, {}, default=False)")
    assert res_false["flag"].dtype == pl.Boolean
    assert list(res_false["flag"]) == [False, False, False]

    res_true = df.mutate("flag = map(post_crm_brr, {}, True)")
    assert res_true["flag"].dtype == pl.Boolean
    assert list(res_true["flag"]) == [True, True, True]

# FILE: tests/test_fillna.py
################################################################################
from __future__ import annotations

import math

import pandas as pd
import polars as pl
import pytest

import pytae as pt


def test_df_fillna_scalar_default_nans_true():
    # Both NaN and null are filled by default
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "flt": [1.0, float("nan"), None],
            "txt": ["a", None, "c"],
            "num": [10, None, 30],
        }
    )
    res = df.fillna(0.0)
    assert res["flt"].to_list() == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    # String column untouched because 0.0 is float
    assert res["txt"].to_list() == ["a", None, "c"]
    assert res["num"].to_list() == [10.0, 0.0, 30.0]


def test_df_fillna_scalar_nans_false():
    # Only null is filled; NaN remains intact
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "flt": [1.0, float("nan"), None],
            "txt": ["a", None, "c"],
        }
    )
    res = df.fillna(0.0, nans=False)
    flt_vals = res["flt"].to_list()
    assert flt_vals[0] == 1.0
    assert math.isnan(flt_vals[1])
    assert flt_vals[2] == 0.0


def test_df_fillna_dict():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "flt": [1.0, float("nan"), None],
            "txt": ["a", None, "c"],
            "num": [10, None, 30],
        }
    )
    res = df.fillna({"flt": -1.0, "txt": "MISSING", "num": 0})
    assert res["flt"].to_list() == [1.0, -1.0, -1.0]
    assert res["txt"].to_list() == ["a", "MISSING", "c"]
    assert res["num"].to_list() == [10, 0, 30]


def test_df_fillna_subset_and_cols():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "flt1": [1.0, float("nan"), None],
            "flt2": [2.0, float("nan"), None],
        }
    )
    # Target flt1 only via *cols
    r1 = df.fillna(0.0, "flt1")
    assert r1["flt1"].to_list() == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    assert math.isnan(r1["flt2"].to_list()[1])
    assert r1["flt2"].to_list()[2] is None

    # Target flt2 only via subset=
    r2 = df.fillna(99.0, subset=["flt2"])
    assert r2["flt2"].to_list() == [2.0, 99.0, 99.0]
    assert math.isnan(r2["flt1"].to_list()[1])


def test_df_fillna_missing_column_raises_key_error():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]})
    with pytest.raises(KeyError, match="fillna: column\\(s\\) \\['non_existent'\\] not found"):
        df.fillna(0, "non_existent")


def test_df_fillna_missing_value_raises_type_error():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]})
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="fillna\\(\\) missing required argument: 'value'"):
        df.fillna()


def test_df_fill_null_and_fill_nan():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "flt": [1.0, float("nan"), None],
        }
    )
    # fill_null fills null only (nans=False)
    r_null = df.fill_null(0.0)
    assert math.isnan(r_null["flt"].to_list()[1])
    assert r_null["flt"].to_list()[2] == 0.0

    # fill_nan fills NaN only, leaving null intact
    r_nan = df.fill_nan(0.0)
    assert r_nan["flt"].to_list()[0] == 1.0
    assert r_nan["flt"].to_list()[1] == 0.0
    assert r_nan["flt"].to_list()[2] is None


def test_functional_and_accessor_fillna():
    # 1. Polars accessor
    pldf = pl.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, float("nan"), None]})
    res_pl = pldf.pt.fillna(0.0)
    assert isinstance(res_pl, pt.DataFrame)
    assert res_pl["x"].to_list() == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]

    # 2. Pandas accessor
    pddf = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, float("nan"), None]})
    res_pd = pddf.pt.fillna(0.0)
    assert isinstance(res_pd, pt.DataFrame)
    assert res_pd["x"].to_list() == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]

    # 3. Top-level pt.fillna
    res_fn = pt.fillna(pldf, 5.0)
    assert res_fn["x"].to_list() == [1.0, 5.0, 5.0]


def test_grouped_dataframe_fillna():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "grp": ["A", "A", "B", "B"],
            "val": [1.0, float("nan"), None, 4.0],
        }
    )
    res = df.by("grp").fillna(0.0)
    assert res["val"].to_list() == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 4.0]

import os

_SRC = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../src"))


def test_import_does_not_load_plotting_shape_or_samples():
    code = (
        r"""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, %r)
import pytae

assert "pytae.plotting" not in sys.modules
assert "pytae.shape" not in sys.modules
assert "matplotlib" not in sys.modules
assert "duckdb" not in sys.modules
assert pytae._cache == {}
assert "penguins" in pytae.sample_data
assert list(pytae.sample_data.keys())
assert pytae._cache == {}

# keys() returns a plain readable tuple, not a bare KeysView object
keys = pytae.sample_data.keys()
assert isinstance(keys, tuple)
assert "penguins" in keys

df = pytae.sample("penguins")
assert len(df) > 0
# sample() returns a copy each time, so mutating it never poisons the cache
assert pytae.sample_data["penguins"] is not df
df.iloc[0, 0] = "MUTATED"
assert pytae.sample_data["penguins"].iloc[0, 0] != "MUTATED"

long = pytae.long
assert long is not None

assert callable(pytae.mutate)
assert hasattr(__import__("pandas").DataFrame, "pt")
assert not hasattr(__import__("pandas").DataFrame, "mutate")

Plotter = pytae.Plotter
assert "pytae.plotting" in sys.modules
assert Plotter is not None
"""
        % _SRC
    )
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-c", code])

    code = (

sys.path.insert(0, %r)

assert "pytae.shape" not in sys.modules
assert callable(__import__("pytae", fromlist=["filter"]).filter)

DF = sys.modules["pandas"].DataFrame

if hasattr(DF, "select"):

"""
        % _SRC
    )
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-c", code])


def test_plotter_import_error_mentions_plot_extra():
    code = (
        r"""
import builtins
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, %r)
real_import = builtins.__import__

def blocked(name, *args, **kwargs):
    if name == "matplotlib" or name.startswith("matplotlib."):
        raise ImportError("No module named matplotlib")
    return real_import(name, *args, **kwargs)

builtins.__import__ = blocked
import pytae
try:
    pytae.Plotter
except ImportError as exc:
    msg = str(exc)
    assert "matplotlib" in msg
    assert "pytae[plot]" in msg
else:
    raise AssertionError("expected ImportError")
"""
        % _SRC
    )
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-c", code])

# FILE: tests/test_join_concat.py
################################################################################
"""Tests for Pytae library join, concat, and transparent Polars method delegation."""

import os
import sys

import pandas as pd
import polars as pl

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../src")))

import pytae as pt


def test_df_join_inner_and_chaining():
    df1 = pt.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "name": ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"], "score": [80, 95, 70]})
    df2 = pt.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3, 4], "dept": ["Eng", "HR", "Sales"]})

    # Join and continue chaining Pytae fluent verbs
    res = df1.join(df2, on="id", how="inner").filter("score >= 80").mutate(score_bonus="score + 10").arrange("score desc")
    assert isinstance(res, pt.DataFrame)
    assert list(res.columns) == ["id", "name", "score", "dept", "score_bonus"]
    assert len(res) == 1
    assert res.iloc[0, "name"] == "Bob"
    assert res.iloc[0, "score_bonus"] == 105


def test_df_join_all_strategies():
    left = pt.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "val": ["a", "b", "c"]})
    right = pt.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3, 4], "score": [20, 30, 40]})

    # left join
    lj = left.join(right, on="id", how="left")
    assert len(lj) == 3
    assert set(lj["id"].to_list()) == {1, 2, 3}

    # right join
    rj = left.join(right, on="id", how="right")
    assert len(rj) == 3
    assert set(rj["id"].to_list()) == {2, 3, 4}

    # full join
    fj = left.join(right, on="id", how="full")
    assert len(fj) == 4
    assert set(fj["id"].to_list()) == {1, 2, 3, 4}

    # semi join (filtering join - returns left rows that match right)
    sj = left.join(right, on="id", how="semi")
    assert len(sj) == 2
    assert list(sj.columns) == ["id", "val"]
    assert set(sj["id"].to_list()) == {2, 3}

    # anti join (returns left rows that do NOT match right)
    aj = left.join(right, on="id", how="anti")
    assert len(aj) == 1
    assert list(aj.columns) == ["id", "val"]
    assert aj.iloc[0, "id"] == 1

    # cross join
    cj = left.join(right, how="cross")
    assert len(cj) == 9  # 3 * 3


def test_df_join_colon_syntax():
    df1 = pt.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "name": ["A", "B", "C"]})
    df2 = pt.DataFrame({"user_id": [2, 3, 4], "role": ["Dev", "PM", "QA"]})

    res = df1.join(df2, on="id:user_id", how="inner")
    assert len(res) == 2
    assert "id" in res.columns
    assert "user_id" in res.columns
    assert "role" in res.columns


def test_df_join_auto_detect_common_columns():
    df1 = pt.DataFrame({"user_id": [1, 2], "score": [90, 85]})
    df2 = pt.DataFrame({"user_id": [2, 3], "grade": ["A", "B"]})

    # Omit on parameter: automatically joins on user_id
    res = df1.join(df2)
    assert len(res) == 1
    assert res.iloc[0, "user_id"] == 2
    assert res.iloc[0, "score"] == 85
    assert res.iloc[0, "grade"] == "A"


def test_top_level_pt_join():
    df1 = pt.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2], "x": [10, 20]})
    df2 = pt.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3], "y": [200, 300]})

    res = pt.join(df1, df2, on="id", how="left")
    assert isinstance(res, pt.DataFrame)
    assert len(res) == 2


def test_pt_accessor_join_pandas_and_polars():
    pdf1 = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2], "v": ["a", "b"]})
    pdf2 = pd.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3], "w": ["x", "y"]})

    # Pandas accessor .pt.join()
    res_pandas = pdf1.pt.join(pdf2, on="id", how="inner")
    assert isinstance(res_pandas, pt.DataFrame)
    assert len(res_pandas) == 1
    assert res_pandas.iloc[0, "id"] == 2

    # Polars accessor .pt.join()
    pldf1 = pl.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2], "v": ["a", "b"]})
    pldf2 = pl.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3], "w": ["x", "y"]})
    res_polars = pldf1.pt.join(pldf2, on="id", how="inner")
    assert isinstance(res_polars, pt.DataFrame)
    assert len(res_polars) == 1


def test_lazy_join_preserves_lazy_execution():
    lf1 = pl.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "val": [10, 20, 30]}).lazy()
    lf2 = pl.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3, 4], "bonus": [100, 200, 300]}).lazy()

    df_lazy1 = pt.DataFrame(lf1)
    df_lazy2 = pt.DataFrame(lf2)

    joined_lazy = df_lazy1.join(df_lazy2, on="id", how="inner").filter("val > 10")
    assert joined_lazy.is_lazy

    collected = joined_lazy.collect()
    assert isinstance(collected, pt.DataFrame)
    assert not collected.is_lazy
    assert len(collected) == 2


def test_concat_vertical_and_fallback():
    df1 = pt.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": ["x", "y"]})
    df2 = pt.DataFrame({"a": [3, 4], "b": ["w", "z"]})
    df3 = pt.DataFrame({"a": [5, 6], "c": [100, 200]})

    # Top-level concat with matching schemas
    res1 = pt.concat([df1, df2])
    assert len(res1) == 4
    assert list(res1.columns) == ["a", "b"]

    # Method chain concat
    res2 = df1.concat(df2)
    assert len(res2) == 4

    # Top-level concat with differing schemas (diagonal_relaxed fallback)
    res3 = pt.concat([df1, df3])
    assert len(res3) == 4
    assert list(res3.columns) == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert res3.iloc[0, "c"] is None
    assert res3.iloc[2, "b"] is None


def test_concat_horizontal():
    df1 = pt.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": ["x", "y"]})
    df2 = pt.DataFrame({"c": [10, 20], "d": [True, False]})

    res = pt.concat([df1, df2], how="horizontal")
    assert len(res) == 2
    assert list(res.columns) == ["a", "b", "c", "d"]


def test_dynamic_polars_forwarding_in_chain():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3, 4], "amt": [10, 25, 30, 45], "cat": ["a", "b", "a", "b"]})

    # with_columns is a native Polars method!
    # Because of transparent forwarding, it executes and wraps result back into pytae.DataFrame:
    res = (
        df.with_columns(tax=pl.col("amt") * 0.1).filter("tax > 2").by("cat").mutate(total="sum(amt)").arrange("total desc")
    )
    assert isinstance(res, pt.DataFrame)
    assert "tax" in res.columns
    assert "total" in res.columns

    # Native slice method
    sliced = df.slice(1, 2)
    assert isinstance(sliced, pt.DataFrame)
    assert len(sliced) == 2

    # Native describe method
    desc = df.describe()
    assert isinstance(desc, pt.DataFrame)
    assert "statistic" in desc.columns

    # Non-DataFrame return (scalar)
    n_unique = df.n_unique()
    assert isinstance(n_unique, int)
    assert n_unique == 4

# FILE: tests/test_lazy.py

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl
import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../src")))

import pytae as pt


@pytest.fixture
def sample_csv(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    csv_file = tmp_path / "sample.csv"
    csv_file.write_text(
        "id,group,score,comment\n"
        "1,alpha,10.5,good\n"
        "2,beta,20.0,better\n"
        "3,alpha,15.5,best\n"
        "4,beta,30.0,great\n"
        "5,alpha,,missing\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    return csv_file


@pytest.fixture
def sample_parquet(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    pq_file = tmp_path / "sample.parquet"
    df = pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "id": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
            "category": ["A", "B", "A", "B", "C"],
            "val1": [10, 20, 30, 40, 50],
            "val2": [100.0, 200.0, 300.0, 400.0, 500.0],
        }
    )
    df.write_parquet(pq_file)
    return pq_file


def test_scan_csv(sample_csv: Path):
    df = pt.scan_csv(sample_csv)
    assert df.is_lazy
    assert "id" in df.columns
    assert "score" in df.columns
    assert df.shape == (5, 4)

    # Chaining preserves laziness
    filtered = df.filter("score > 12")
    assert filtered.is_lazy

    mutated = filtered.mutate(doubled="score * 2")
    assert mutated.is_lazy

    arranged = mutated.arrange("doubled desc")
    assert arranged.is_lazy

    selected = arranged.select("id", "group", "doubled")
    assert selected.is_lazy

    # Materialize
    collected = selected.collect()
    assert not collected.is_lazy
    assert list(collected.columns) == ["id", "group", "doubled"]
    assert len(collected) == 3
    assert collected["doubled"].to_list() == [60.0, 40.0, 31.0]


def test_scan_parquet(sample_parquet: Path):
    df = pt.scan_parquet(sample_parquet)
    assert df.is_lazy
    assert df.columns == ["id", "category", "val1", "val2"]
    assert df.shape == (5, 4)
    assert len(df) == 5

    res = (
        df.filter("category in ['A', 'B']")
        .mutate(total="val1 + val2")
        .arrange("total desc")
        .select("id", "total")
        .collect()
    )
    assert not res.is_lazy
    assert len(res) == 4
    assert res["total"].to_list() == [440.0, 330.0, 220.0, 110.0]


def test_lazy_explain(sample_parquet: Path):
    df = pt.scan_parquet(sample_parquet).filter("val1 > 20").select("id", "category")
    assert df.is_lazy
    explanation = df.explain()
    assert isinstance(explanation, str)
    assert "FILTER" in explanation or "SELECT" in explanation or "val1" in explanation


def test_lazy_conversion():
    eager_df = pt.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2, 3], "y": [4, 5, 6]})
    assert not eager_df.is_lazy

    lazy_df = eager_df.lazy()
    assert lazy_df.is_lazy

    # Collecting returns eager pt.DataFrame
    back = lazy_df.collect()
    assert not back.is_lazy
    assert back["x"].to_list() == [1, 2, 3]


def test_lazy_verbs(sample_parquet: Path):
    df = pt.scan_parquet(sample_parquet)

    # distinct
    d = df.distinct("category")
    assert d.is_lazy
    assert len(d.collect()) == 3

    # dropna (Zero-Data-Loss safety defaults: bare defaults to how='all', targeted to how='any')
    assert len(df.dropna().collect()) == 5

    dn = df.dropna("val1")
    assert dn.is_lazy
    assert len(dn.collect()) == 5
    assert len(df.dropna(how="any").collect()) == 5

    # arrange + head
    p = df.arrange("val1 desc").head(2)
    assert p.is_lazy
    assert len(p.collect()) == 2
    assert p.collect()["val1"].to_list() == [50, 40]

    # fillna
    fn = df.fillna(0)
    assert fn.is_lazy
    assert len(fn.collect()) == 5

    # clean_columns
    cc = df.clean_columns(case="upper")
    assert cc.is_lazy
    assert "CATEGORY" in cc.collect().columns


def test_lazy_grouped_operations(sample_parquet: Path):
    df = pt.scan_parquet(sample_parquet)

    # Grouped mutate on LazyFrame
    g_mut = df.by("category").mutate(mean_val1="mean(val1)")
    assert g_mut.is_lazy
    collected_mut = g_mut.collect()
    assert "mean_val1" in collected_mut.columns

    # Grouped agg on LazyFrame
    g_agg = df.by("category").agg(sum_val1="val1:sum", mean_val2="val2:mean")
    assert g_agg.is_lazy
    collected_agg = g_agg.collect()
    assert "sum_val1" in collected_agg.columns
    assert "mean_val2" in collected_agg.columns
    assert len(collected_agg) == 3


def test_lazy_sinking(tmp_path: Path, sample_parquet: Path):
    df = pt.scan_parquet(sample_parquet).filter("val1 >= 30")
    assert df.is_lazy

    out_pq = tmp_path / "output.parquet"
    df.to_parquet(out_pq)
    assert out_pq.exists()
    assert len(pl.read_parquet(out_pq)) == 3

    out_csv = tmp_path / "output.csv"
    df.to_csv(out_csv)
    assert out_csv.exists()
    assert len(pl.read_csv(out_csv)) == 3


def test_cli_lazy_execution(sample_parquet: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    out_file = tmp_path / "cli_out.csv"
    # Run CLI using python module
    cmd = [
        sys.executable,

        "calc = val1 * 10",

def test_read_and_scan_deprecation():
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError, match="pt.read\\(\\) has been removed; use pt.read_parquet"):
        pt.read("some_file.parquet")

    with pytest.raises(AttributeError, match="pt.scan\\(\\) has been removed; use pt.scan_parquet"):

def test_lazy_fillna():
    ldf = pl.LazyFrame({"x": [1.0, float("nan"), None], "y": ["A", None, "B"]})
    df = pt.DataFrame(ldf)
    assert df.is_lazy

    filled = df.fillna(0.0)
    assert filled.is_lazy
    collected = filled.collect()
    assert collected["x"].to_list() == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    assert collected["y"].to_list() == ["A", None, "B"]

    # Dict fill on lazy frame
    d_filled = df.fillna({"x": 99.0, "y": "MISSING"})
    assert d_filled.is_lazy
    c2 = d_filled.collect()
    assert c2["x"].to_list() == [1.0, 99.0, 99.0]
    assert c2["y"].to_list() == ["A", "MISSING", "B"]

# FILE: tests/test_mask.py
################################################################################
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import polars as pl
import pytest

import pytae as pt
from pytae.mask import parse_mask_spec, parse_unmask_spec


def test_parse_mask_spec():
    assert parse_mask_spec("email=hash, ssn=redact") == {"email": "hash", "ssn": "redact"}
    assert parse_mask_spec("email:hash, ssn:encrypt") == {"email": "hash", "ssn": "encrypt"}
    assert parse_mask_spec("email, ssn", default_method="hash") == {"email": "hash", "ssn": "hash"}
    assert parse_mask_spec({"email": "sha256", "user": "token"}) == {"email": "hash", "user": "tokenize"}
    assert parse_mask_spec(email="encrypt", ssn="redact") == {"email": "encrypt", "ssn": "redact"}

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="unknown mask method 'banana'"):
        parse_mask_spec("email=banana")


def test_parse_unmask_spec():
    assert parse_unmask_spec("email, ssn") == ["email", "ssn"]
    assert parse_unmask_spec(["email", "ssn"]) == ["email", "ssn"]
    assert parse_unmask_spec("email", "ssn") == ["email", "ssn"]


def test_mask_one_way_hash_and_salt():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "email": ["alice@td.com", "bob@td.com", None],
            "id": [1, 2, None],
        }
    )

    # Default hash without salt
    m1 = df.mask("email=hash")
    assert m1["email"][0] is not None
    assert len(m1["email"][0]) == 64  # SHA-256 hex length
    assert m1["email"][2] is None  # Preserves null

    # Hash with salt
    m2 = df.mask("email=hash", salt="custom_salt")
    assert m2["email"][0] != m1["email"][0]
    assert m2["email"][2] is None

    # Determinism: same value produces same hash
    m_dup = df.mask("email=hash", salt="custom_salt")
    assert m_dup["email"][0] == m2["email"][0]


def test_mask_one_way_redact():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "ssn": ["123-45-6789", "987-65-4321", None],
            "notes": ["secret A", "secret B", None],
        }
    )

    m = df.mask("ssn=redact, notes=redact")
    assert m["ssn"].to_list() == ["***", "***", None]
    assert m["notes"].to_list() == ["***", "***", None]

    # Custom redact string
    m_custom = df.mask("ssn=redact", redact_val="[CONFIDENTIAL]")
    assert m_custom["ssn"].to_list() == ["[CONFIDENTIAL]", "[CONFIDENTIAL]", None]


def test_mask_option_1_key_encrypt_and_unmask():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "user": ["Alice", "Bob", None],
            "ssn": ["111-22-3333", "444-55-6666", None],
        }
    )

    key = "TestSecretKey!2026"
    masked = df.mask("user=encrypt, ssn=encrypt", key=key)

    # Values are scrambled
    assert masked["user"][0] != "Alice"
    assert masked["user"][1] != "Bob"
    assert masked["user"][2] is None

    # Unmask with correct key
    unmasked = masked.unmask("user, ssn", key=key)
    assert unmasked["user"].to_list() == ["Alice", "Bob", None]
    assert unmasked["ssn"].to_list() == ["111-22-3333", "444-55-6666", None]

    # Unmask with WRONG key raises clear error
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="decryption failed"):
        masked.unmask("user", key="WrongPassword")


def test_mask_option_2_vault_tokenize_and_unmask(tmp_path: Path):
    vault_file = tmp_path / "vault.parquet"

    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "name": ["Alice", "Bob", "Alice", None],
            "emp_id": [101, 102, 101, None],
        }
    )

    # Tokenize name and emp_id
    masked = df.mask("name=tokenize, emp_id=tokenize", vault=vault_file)
    assert vault_file.exists()

    # Repeated values get identical tokens
    assert masked["name"][0] == masked["name"][2]
    assert masked["name"][0] != masked["name"][1]
    assert masked["name"][3] is None

    # Check vault file content
    vault_df = pl.read_parquet(vault_file)
    assert set(vault_df.columns) == {"column", "token", "original", "dtype"}
    assert len(vault_df) == 4  # 2 unique names + 2 unique emp_ids

    # Unmask from vault restores exact values and types
    unmasked = masked.unmask("name, emp_id", vault=vault_file)
    assert unmasked["name"].to_list() == ["Alice", "Bob", "Alice", None]
    assert unmasked["emp_id"].to_list() == [101, 102, 101, None]


def test_mask_option_2_vault_incremental_append(tmp_path: Path):
    vault_file = tmp_path / "vault.json"

    # Batch 1
    df1 = pt.DataFrame({"name": ["Alice", "Bob"]})
    m1 = df1.mask("name=tokenize", vault=vault_file)
    tok_alice = m1["name"][0]
    tok_bob = m1["name"][1]

    # Batch 2 (contains Alice again + new user Charlie)
    df2 = pt.DataFrame({"name": ["Alice", "Charlie"]})
    m2 = df2.mask("name=tokenize", vault=vault_file)

    # Alice gets the exact same token from batch 1
    assert m2["name"][0] == tok_alice
    # Charlie gets a new token distinct from Alice and Bob
    assert m2["name"][1] not in (tok_alice, tok_bob)

    # Both batches unmask cleanly
    unm1 = m1.unmask("name", vault=vault_file)
    unm2 = m2.unmask("name", vault=vault_file)
    assert unm1["name"].to_list() == ["Alice", "Bob"]
    assert unm2["name"].to_list() == ["Alice", "Charlie"]


def test_mask_combined_options(tmp_path: Path):
    vault_file = tmp_path / "multi_vault.parquet"
    key = "MultiPass456"

    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "user": ["Alice", "Bob"],
            "ssn": ["111", "222"],
            "email": ["a@a.com", "b@b.com"],
            "notes": ["note 1", "note 2"],
        }
    )

    # Combine all 4 methods: tokenize, encrypt, hash, redact
    masked = df.mask(
        "user=tokenize, ssn=encrypt, email=hash, notes=redact",
        key=key,
        vault=vault_file,
    )

    assert masked["user"][0].startswith("user_")
    assert masked["ssn"][0] != "111"
    assert len(masked["email"][0]) == 64
    assert masked["notes"].to_list() == ["***", "***"]

    # Unmask both user (via vault) and ssn (via key) in a single call
    unmasked = masked.unmask("user, ssn", key=key, vault=vault_file)
    assert unmasked["user"].to_list() == ["Alice", "Bob"]
    assert unmasked["ssn"].to_list() == ["111", "222"]
    # email and notes remain safely masked
    assert len(unmasked["email"][0]) == 64
    assert unmasked["notes"].to_list() == ["***", "***"]


def test_mask_pandas_accessor(tmp_path: Path):
    pdf = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "name": ["Alice", "Bob"],
            "ssn": ["111", "222"],
        }
    )

    key = "PandasKey789"
    # df.pt.mask
    m_pt = pdf.pt.mask("name=hash, ssn=encrypt", key=key)
    assert len(m_pt["name"][0]) == 64

    # df.pt.unmask
    unm_pt = m_pt.pt.unmask("ssn", key=key)
    assert list(unm_pt["ssn"]) == ["111", "222"]


def test_mask_validation_errors():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"name": ["Alice"]})

    # Encrypt without key
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="requires -key/--key"):
        df.mask("name=encrypt")

    # Tokenize without vault
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="requires -vault/--vault"):
        df.mask("name=tokenize")

    # Unmask without key or vault
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="requires -key/--key .* and/or -vault/--vault"):
        df.unmask("name")

import os
import sys

import pandas as pd
import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../src")))

import pytae as pt
from pytae._parsing import parse_mutate_spec


def _df():
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "species": ["Adelie", "Gentoo"],
            "body_mass_g": [3000.0, 4000.0],
            "bill_length_mm": [30.0, 40.0],
        }
    )


def test_mutate_basic_expression():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), bmi="body_mass_g / bill_length_mm ** 2")
    assert list(result["bmi"]) == [pytest.approx(3.333333, rel=1e-4), pytest.approx(2.5)]


def test_mutate_multiple_entries_in_one_call():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), heavy="body_mass_g > 3500", mass_kg="body_mass_g / 1000")
    assert list(result["heavy"]) == [False, True]
    assert list(result["mass_kg"]) == [3.0, 4.0]


def test_mutate_later_entry_references_earlier_one():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), mass_kg="body_mass_g / 1000", mass_lb="mass_kg * 2.20462")
    assert result["mass_lb"].iloc[0] == pytest.approx(6.61386)


def test_mutate_string_comparison_needs_quotes():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), is_adelie="species == 'Adelie'")
    assert list(result["is_adelie"]) == [True, False]


def test_mutate_does_not_modify_original():
    df = _df()
    pt.mutate(df, bmi="body_mass_g / bill_length_mm ** 2")
    assert "bmi" not in df.columns


def test_mutate_overwrites_existing_column():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), body_mass_g="body_mass_g / 1000")
    assert list(result["body_mass_g"]) == [3.0, 4.0]


def test_mutate_unknown_column_suggests_typo():
    with pytest.raises(KeyError, match="did you mean 'body_mass_g'"):
        pt.mutate(_df(), bmi="bod_mass_g / bill_length_mm")


def test_mutate_quoting_column_reference_breaks_arithmetic():
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        pt.mutate(_df(), bmi="'body_mass_g' / 'bill_length_mm' ** 2")


def test_mutate_empty_spec_errors():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="mutate\\(\\) expects at least one"):
        pt.mutate(_df())


def test_mutate_if_else_basic():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), size="if_else(body_mass_g >= 3500, 'heavy', 'light')")
    assert list(result["size"]) == ["light", "heavy"]


def test_mutate_if_else_numeric_values():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), bonus="if_else(body_mass_g >= 3500, 100, 10)")
    assert list(result["bonus"]) == [10, 100]


def test_mutate_if_else_value_can_be_column_expression():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), adjusted="if_else(body_mass_g >= 3500, body_mass_g / 1000, body_mass_g)")
    assert list(result["adjusted"]) == [3000.0, 4.0]


def test_mutate_if_else_wrong_arg_count_errors():
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        pt.mutate(_df(), size="if_else(body_mass_g >= 3500, 'heavy')")


def test_mutate_if_else_mixed_dtype_branches():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), g="if_else(body_mass_g >= 3500, 'heavy', 0)")
    assert list(result["g"]) in ([0, "heavy"], ["0", "heavy"])


def test_mutate_case_when_mixed_dtype_choices():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), g="case_when((body_mass_g >= 3500, 'heavy'), 0)")
    assert list(result["g"]) in ([0, "heavy"], ["0", "heavy"])


def test_mutate_case_when_first_match_wins():
    result = pt.mutate(
        _df(),
        grade="case_when((body_mass_g >= 3800, 'A'), (body_mass_g >= 3200, 'B'), 'C')",
    )
    assert list(result["grade"]) == ["C", "A"]


def test_mutate_case_when_no_default_gives_nan_for_unmatched():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), grade="case_when((body_mass_g >= 3800, 'A'))")
    assert result["grade"].iloc[1] == "A"
    assert pd.isna(result["grade"].iloc[0])


def test_mutate_case_when_default_must_be_last():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="case_when default .*must be the last argument"):
        pt.mutate(_df(), grade="case_when('C', (body_mass_g >= 3800, 'A'))")


def test_mutate_case_when_requires_at_least_one_entry():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="case_when expects at least one"):
        pt.mutate(_df(), grade="case_when()")


def test_mutate_if_else_and_case_when_chain_with_other_entries():
    result = pt.mutate(
        _df(),
        mass_kg="body_mass_g / 1000",
        size="if_else(mass_kg >= 3.5, 'heavy', 'light')",
    )
    assert list(result["size"]) == ["light", "heavy"]


def test_mutate_local_var_reference():

    result = pt.mutate(_df(), heavy="body_mass_g >= @threshold")
    assert list(result["heavy"]) == [False, True]


def test_mutate_local_var_reference_via_accessor():

    assert list(result["heavy"]) == [False, True]


def test_mutate_local_var_reference_in_if_else():
    threshold = 3500.0
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), size="if_else(body_mass_g >= @threshold, 'heavy', 'light')")
    assert list(result["size"]) == ["light", "heavy"]


def test_mutate_local_var_select_columns_in_if_else():
    df = pt.DataFrame({
        "cola": [10, 20, 30],
        "colb": [100, 200, 300],
    })
    var = "yes"
    res1 = df.mutate('colx = if_else(@var == "yes", cola, colb)')
    assert list(res1["colx"]) == [10, 20, 30]

    var = "no"
    res2 = df.mutate('colx = if_else(@var == "yes", cola, colb)')
    assert list(res2["colx"]) == [100, 200, 300]


def test_mutate_local_var_reference_in_case_when():
    low, high = 3200.0, 3800.0
    result = pt.mutate(
        _df(),
        grade="case_when((body_mass_g >= @high, 'A'), (body_mass_g >= @low, 'B'), 'C')",
    )
    assert list(result["grade"]) == ["C", "A"]


def test_mutate_unknown_local_var_suggests_typo_free_error():

    df = _df()

    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="unexpected positional argument"):

def test_mutate_bracketed_and_backtick_columns_in_fallback():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"col a": [10, 20], "col b": [1, 2]})
    res1 = pt.mutate(df, c="if_else([col a] > 15, 'high', 'low')")
    assert list(res1["c"]) == ["low", "high"]
    res2 = pt.mutate(df, c="if_else(`col a` > 15, 'high', 'low')")
    assert list(res2["c"]) == ["low", "high"]
    res3 = pt.mutate(df, total="[col a] + [col b]")
    assert list(res3["total"]) == [11, 22]


def test_parse_mutate_spec_equals_and_comments():

    res = parse_mutate_spec(spec)

    assert "mass_lb" in res
    assert res["mass_kg"] == "body_mass_g / 1000"

def test_mutate_bracketed_columns():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"body mass g": [3000.0, 4000.0], "height": [1.5, 2.0]})
    # Target column has brackets, source has brackets
    res1 = df.pt.mutate("[mass kg] = [body mass g] / 1000")
    assert "mass kg" in res1.columns
    assert list(res1["mass kg"]) == [3.0, 4.0]

    res2 = df.pt.mutate("[bmi score] = [body mass g] / (height ** 2)")

def test_mutate_grouped_single_col():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["a", "a", "b"], "val": [10.0, 20.0, 60.0]})
    res = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate(
        "avg = mean(val), diff = val - avg, total = sum(val), cnt = n, cnt2 = n()",
    )
    assert list(res["avg"]) == [15.0, 15.0, 60.0]
    assert list(res["diff"]) == [-5.0, 5.0, 0.0]
    assert list(res["total"]) == [30.0, 30.0, 60.0]
    assert list(res["cnt"]) == [2, 2, 1]
    assert list(res["cnt2"]) == [2, 2, 1]


def test_mutate_grouped_multi_col():
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "g1": ["a", "a", "a", "b"],
            "g2": ["x", "x", "y", "x"],
            "val": [10.0, 30.0, 5.0, 100.0],
        }
    )
    res1 = df.pt.by("g1", "g2").pt.mutate("m = mean(val), cnt = n")
    assert list(res1["m"]) == [20.0, 20.0, 5.0, 100.0]
    assert list(res1["cnt"]) == [2, 2, 1, 1]

    # Positional pt.by with multiple columns
    res2 = pt.mutate(pt.by(df, "g1", "g2"), "m = mean(val)")
    assert list(res2["m"]) == [20.0, 20.0, 5.0, 100.0]


def test_mutate_grouped_spaced_brackets():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"group code": ["a", "a", "b"], "total bill": [10.0, 30.0, 50.0]})
    res = df.pt.by("group code").pt.mutate("[diff bill] = [total bill] - mean([total bill])")
    assert list(res["diff bill"]) == [-10.0, 10.0, 0.0]


def test_mutate_grouped_dropna_observed():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["a", None, "a"], "val": [10.0, 50.0, 30.0]})
    # Default is dropna=False: computes on the NA group
    res_default = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate("m = mean(val)")
    assert res_default["m"].iloc[1] == 50.0
    assert res_default["m"].iloc[0] == 20.0
    assert res_default["m"].iloc[2] == 20.0

    res_dropna = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate("m = mean(val)", dropna=True)
    assert pd.isna(res_dropna["m"].iloc[1])
    assert res_dropna["m"].iloc[0] == 20.0
    assert res_dropna["m"].iloc[2] == 20.0

    res_keepna = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate("m = mean(val)", dropna=False)
    assert res_keepna["m"].iloc[1] == 50.0


def test_mutate_grouped_duplicate_index():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["a", "b", "a"], "val": [10.0, 50.0, 30.0]}, index=[0, 1, 0])
    res = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate("m = mean(val)")
    assert list(res["m"]) == [20.0, 50.0, 20.0]
    assert list(res.index) == [0, 1, 0]


def test_mutate_grouped_functional_and_callable():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["a", "a", "b"], "val": [10.0, 20.0, 60.0]})
    # Functional pt.mutate
    res1 = pt.mutate(pt.by(df, "grp"), "avg = mean(val)")
    assert list(res1["avg"]) == [15.0, 15.0, 60.0]

    # Callable inside grouped mutate
    res2 = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate(half_mean=lambda g: g["val"].mean() / 2)
    assert list(res2["half_mean"]) == [7.5, 7.5, 30.0]


def test_mutate_rejects_by_arg():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["a", "b"], "val": [1, 2]})
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="df.pt.mutate\\(\\) does not accept 'by'"):
        df.pt.mutate("m = mean(val)", by="grp")
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="mutate\\(\\) does not accept 'by'"):
        pt.mutate(df, "m = mean(val)", by="grp")


def test_mutate_coalesce_scalar_broadcast():

def test_mutate_map_preserves_explicit_null():
    # Lib Issue 11
    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": ["x", "y", "z"]})
    res = pt.mutate(df, b="map(a, {'x': 1, 'y': None}, -1)")

def test_mutate_if_else_and_case_when_nullable_boolean():
    # Lib Issue 12
    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": pd.Series([1, pd.NA, 3], dtype="Int64")})
    res_if = pt.mutate(df, b="if_else(a > 2, 'y', 'n')")
    assert list(res_if["b"]) == ["n", "n", "y"]

    res_cw = pt.mutate(df, b="case_when((a > 2, 'y'), 'n')")
    assert list(res_cw["b"]) == ["n", "n", "y"]


def test_mutate_n_row_count_vs_col_and_helper():
    # Lib Issue 16: caller local 'n' does not shadow row count 'n' unless referenced as '@n'
    n = 999  # noqa: F841
    df = pd.DataFrame({"val": [10, 20, 30]})
    res = df.pt.mutate("cnt = n, caller_n = @n")
    assert list(res["cnt"]) == [3, 3, 3]
    assert list(res["caller_n"]) == [999, 999, 999]


def test_mutate_grouped_callable_sees_original_index():
    # Lib Issue 17: callable sees original index in grouped mutate
    s = pd.Series([100, 200, 300], index=[10, 20, 30])
    df = pd.DataFrame({"g": ["a", "b", "a"], "x": [1, 2, 3]}, index=[10, 20, 30])
    res = df.pt.by("g").pt.mutate(y=lambda d: d["x"] + s.reindex(d.index))
    assert list(res["y"]) == [101, 202, 303]
    assert list(res.index) == [10, 20, 30]


def test_mutate_scalar_if_else_and_case_when():
    # Lib Issue 1 (Review 2ec5bbba): scalar condition in if_else and case_when broadcasts across rows and groups
    df = pd.DataFrame({"val": [10, 20, 30]})
    assert df.pt.mutate(y="if_else(n > 1, 1, 0)")["y"].tolist() == [1, 1, 1]
    assert df.pt.mutate(y="case_when((n > 1, 'big'), 'small')")["y"].tolist() == ["big", "big", "big"]

    df2 = pd.DataFrame({"val": [10, 20, 30]}, index=[5, 6, 7])
    assert df2.pt.mutate(y="if_else(n > 1, 1, 0)")["y"].tolist() == [1, 1, 1]

    df3 = pd.DataFrame({"g": ["a", "a", "b"], "val": [10, 20, 30]})
    assert df3.pt.by("g").pt.mutate(y="if_else(n > 1, 1, 0)")["y"].tolist() == [1, 1, 0]


def test_mutate_lit_constant_when_column_exists():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"original": [10, 20], "val": [1, 2]})

    # Without inner quotes, passing source="original" copies the column
    assert list(df.pt.mutate(source="original")["source"]) == [10, 20]

    # With inner quotes source="'original'", assigns literal string
    res_quoted = df.pt.mutate(source="'original'")
    assert list(res_quoted["source"]) == ["original", "original"]

    # Positional string expression with inner quotes
    res_pos = df.pt.mutate("source = 'original'")
    assert list(res_pos["source"]) == ["original", "original"]

    # Grouped mutation with quoted literal
    res_grp = df.pt.by("val").pt.mutate(source="'original'")
    assert list(res_grp["source"]) == ["original", "original"]

    res_grp_str = df.pt.by("val").pt.mutate("source = 'original'")
    assert list(res_grp_str["source"]) == ["original", "original"]

    # Native Python non-string literals (int, float, bool)
    res_num = df.pt.mutate(source=42, flag=True)
    assert list(res_num["source"]) == [42, 42]
    assert list(res_num["flag"]) == [True, True]

    # Calling pt.lit() raises AttributeError pointing to quoted syntax
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError, match="pt.lit\\(\\) has been removed"):
        pt.lit("original")


def test_mutate_grouped_vectorized_all_stats():
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "grp": ["a", "a", "a", "b", "b"],
            "val": [10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 100.0, 200.0],
            "name": ["alice", "bob", "charlie", "dave", "eve"],
        }
    )
    res = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate(
        "avg = mean(val), tot = sum(val), med = median(val), "
        "lo = min(val), hi = max(val), sd = std(val), vr = var(val), "
        "cnt = n, cnt_fn = n(), upper_name = name.str.upper()"
    )
    assert list(res["avg"]) == [20.0, 20.0, 20.0, 150.0, 150.0]
    assert list(res["tot"]) == [60.0, 60.0, 60.0, 300.0, 300.0]
    assert list(res["med"]) == [20.0, 20.0, 20.0, 150.0, 150.0]
    assert list(res["lo"]) == [10.0, 10.0, 10.0, 100.0, 100.0]
    assert list(res["hi"]) == [30.0, 30.0, 30.0, 200.0, 200.0]
    assert list(res["cnt"]) == [3, 3, 3, 2, 2]
    assert list(res["cnt_fn"]) == [3, 3, 3, 2, 2]
    assert list(res["upper_name"]) == ["ALICE", "BOB", "CHARLIE", "DAVE", "EVE"]


def test_mutate_grouped_fallback_series_method():
    # Expressions calling custom Series methods like .cumsum() fall back to per-group evaluation
    df = pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["a", "a", "b", "b"], "val": [1, 2, 10, 20]})
    res = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate("cs = val.cumsum()")
    assert list(res["cs"]) == [1, 3, 10, 30]


def test_mutate_multi_col_in_place_and_chaining():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"rev": [100.0, 200.0], "cost": [40.0, 80.0], "tax": [10.0, 20.0]})
    res = df.pt.mutate("(rev, cost, tax) = _ * 1.5, profit = rev - cost - tax")
    assert list(res["rev"]) == [150.0, 300.0]
    assert list(res["cost"]) == [60.0, 120.0]
    assert list(res["tax"]) == [15.0, 30.0]
    assert list(res["profit"]) == [75.0, 150.0]


def test_mutate_multi_col_suffix_and_prefix():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"rev": [100.0, 200.0], "cost": [50.0, 100.0]})
    res_suf = df.pt.mutate("(rev, cost)_usd = _ * 1.08")
    assert list(res_suf["rev"]) == [100.0, 200.0]
    assert list(res_suf["rev_usd"]) == [pytest.approx(108.0), pytest.approx(216.0)]
    assert list(res_suf["cost_usd"]) == [pytest.approx(54.0), pytest.approx(108.0)]

    res_pre = df.pt.mutate("norm_(rev, cost) = _ / max(_)")
    assert list(res_pre["norm_rev"]) == [0.5, 1.0]
    assert list(res_pre["norm_cost"]) == [0.5, 1.0]


def test_mutate_multi_col_selectors_and_grouped():
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "species": ["Adelie", "Adelie", "Gentoo", "Gentoo"],
            "bill_length_mm": [30.0, 50.0, 40.0, 60.0],
            "bill_depth_mm": [10.0, 20.0, 15.0, 25.0],
        }
    )
    res_sw = df.pt.mutate("(startswith=bill_) = _ / 10")
    assert list(res_sw["bill_length_mm"]) == [3.0, 5.0, 4.0, 6.0]
    assert list(res_sw["bill_depth_mm"]) == [1.0, 2.0, 1.5, 2.5]

    # Grouped dtype=numeric selector (automatically excludes grouping columns)
    res_grp = df.pt.by("species").pt.mutate("(dtype=numeric) = _ - mean(_)")
    assert list(res_grp["bill_length_mm"]) == [-10.0, 10.0, -10.0, 10.0]
    assert list(res_grp["bill_depth_mm"]) == [-5.0, 5.0, -5.0, 5.0]


def test_mutate_multi_col_spaced_columns():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"col a": [10, 20], "col b": [30, 40]})
    res = df.pt.mutate("([col a], [col b]) = _ + 5")
    assert list(res["col a"]) == [15, 25]
    assert list(res["col b"]) == [35, 45]


def test_mutate_map_with_spaced_columns():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"island name": ["Biscoe", "Dream", "Torgersen"]})
    res = df.pt.mutate("[island code] = map([island name], {'Biscoe': 'BIS', 'Dream': 'DRM'}, 'TOR')")
    assert list(res["island code"]) == ["BIS", "DRM", "TOR"]


def test_mutate_disallow_dot_map_method_syntax():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"species": ["Adelie", "Gentoo"], "island name": ["Biscoe", "Dream"]})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="'.map\\(\\)' method syntax is not supported"):
        df.pt.mutate("code = species.map({'Adelie': 'AD'})")

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="'.map\\(\\)' method syntax is not supported"):
        df.pt.mutate("[code] = [island name].map({'Biscoe': 'BIS'})")


def test_mutate_map_column_and_expr_defaults():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "species": ["Adelie", "Gentoo", "Chinstrap"],
            "alt_name": ["Penguin A", "Penguin G", "Penguin C"],
        }
    )
    # 1. Fallback to column itself (preserves unmapped values)
    r1 = df.mutate(mapped="map(species, {'Adelie': 'AD'}, species)")
    assert list(r1["mapped"]) == ["AD", "Gentoo", "Chinstrap"]

    # 2. 2-argument map (unmapped values are preserved)
    r2 = df.mutate(mapped="map(species, {'Adelie': 'AD'})")
    assert list(r2["mapped"]) == ["AD", "Gentoo", "Chinstrap"]

    # 3. Fallback to another column
    r3 = df.mutate(mapped="map(species, {'Adelie': 'AD'}, alt_name)")
    assert list(r3["mapped"]) == ["AD", "Penguin G", "Penguin C"]

    # 4. Keyword default=...
    r4 = df.mutate(mapped="map(species, {'Adelie': 'AD'}, default=species)")
    assert list(r4["mapped"]) == ["AD", "Gentoo", "Chinstrap"]


def test_mutate_smart_fillna():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "flt": [1.0, float("nan"), None],
            "str_col": ["alpha", None, "gamma"],
        }
    )

    # 1. fillna(col, val) -> fills both NaN and null by default (nans=True)
    r1 = df.mutate(clean="fillna(flt, 0.0)")
    assert list(r1["clean"]) == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]

    # 2. fillna(col, val, nans=False) -> fills null only, leaves NaN intact
    r2 = df.mutate(clean="fillna(flt, 0.0, nans=False)")
    assert r2["clean"][0] == 1.0 and str(r2["clean"][1]) == "nan" and r2["clean"][2] == 0.0

    # 3. Method syntax col.fillna(0.0)
    r3 = df.mutate(clean="flt.fillna(0.0)")
    assert list(r3["clean"]) == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]

    # 4. fillna on string column (safely fills null without is_nan error)
    r4 = df.mutate(clean="fillna(str_col, 'MISSING')")
    assert list(r4["clean"]) == ["alpha", "MISSING", "gamma"]

    # 5. Method syntax str_col.fillna('MISSING')
    r5 = df.mutate(clean="str_col.fillna('MISSING')")
    assert list(r5["clean"]) == ["alpha", "MISSING", "gamma"]


def test_fillna_cleans_float_nans():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "flt": [10.0, float("nan"), None, 30.0],
        }
    )
    # df.fillna(0) fills both NaN and null
    cleaned = df.fillna(0.0)
    assert list(cleaned["flt"]) == [10.0, 0.0, 0.0, 30.0]


def test_mutate_dt_and_str_methods():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "dt_str": ["2026-03-15 14:30:00", "2026-04-20 09:15:00"],
            "name": ["john doe", "jane smith"],
        }
    )
    res = df.mutate(
        d="date(dt_str)",
        yr="date(dt_str).dt.year()",
        mo="date(dt_str).dt.month()",
        title_name="name.str.title()",
        rep="name.str.replace('john', 'jack')",
    )
    assert list(res["yr"]) == [2026, 2026]
    assert list(res["mo"]) == [3, 4]
    assert list(res["title_name"]) == ["John Doe", "Jane Smith"]
    assert list(res["rep"]) == ["jack doe", "jane smith"]


def test_mutate_interleaved_callable_and_string_expression():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2, 3]})
    # String expression 'b' references column 'a' created by callable in the same mutate call
    res = df.mutate(a=lambda d: d["x"] * 2, b="a + 10")
    assert list(res["a"]) == [2, 4, 6]
    assert list(res["b"]) == [12, 14, 16]


def test_mutate_interleaved_string_callable_string():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2, 3]})
    # String 'a', Callable 'b' using 'a', String 'c' using 'b'
    res = df.mutate("a = x * 2", b=lambda d: d["a"] + 5, c="b * 10")
    assert list(res["a"]) == [2, 4, 6]
    assert list(res["b"]) == [7, 9, 11]
    assert list(res["c"]) == [70, 90, 110]


def test_mutate_grouped_interleaved_callable_and_string():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"grp": ["k", "k", "m"], "x": [1, 2, 3]})
    # Grouped mutate: callable 'a' then string 'b' referencing 'a'
    res = df.by("grp").mutate(a=lambda g: g["x"] * 2, b="a + 10")
    assert list(res["a"]) == [2, 4, 6]
    assert list(res["b"]) == [12, 14, 16]


def test_mutate_consecutive_callables_consuming_each_other():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2, 3]})
    # One callable consuming another callable's output
    res = df.mutate(
        a=lambda d: d["x"] + 1,
        b=lambda d: d["a"] * 2,
        c=lambda d: d["b"] + 100,
    )
    assert list(res["a"]) == [2, 3, 4]
    assert list(res["b"]) == [4, 6, 8]
    assert list(res["c"]) == [104, 106, 108]


def test_mutate_grouped_consecutive_callables_consuming_each_other():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"grp": ["A", "A", "B"], "x": [1, 2, 10]})
    # Grouped callables consuming each other sequentially
    res = df.by("grp").mutate(
        a=lambda g: g["x"] + 1,
        b=lambda g: g["a"] * 2,
        c=lambda g: g["b"] + 100,
    )
    assert list(res["a"]) == [2, 3, 11]
    assert list(res["b"]) == [4, 6, 22]
    assert list(res["c"]) == [104, 106, 122]


def test_mutate_str_methods_and_null_checks_case_when():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "origin_hub": ["NYC", "LAX", "ORD", "SEA"],
            "dest_code": ["NYC", "MIA-EXP-9", "DAL", "BOS"],
            "hazmat_class": [None, None, "CLASS-3", None],
        }
    )
    res = df.mutate(
        shipping_mode="""
        case_when(
            (origin_hub == dest_code, 'Local Courier'),
            (dest_code.str.contains('-EXP-') | hazmat_class.is_not_null(), 'Special Freight'),
            'Standard Ground'
        )
        """
    )
    assert list(res["shipping_mode"]) == ["Local Courier", "Special Freight", "Special Freight", "Standard Ground"]

    # Also test functional is_not_null and starts_with / ends_with
    res2 = df.mutate(
        is_exp=lambda d: d["dest_code"].str.contains("-EXP-"),
        has_hazmat=df.mutate("has_hazmat = is_not_null(hazmat_class)")["has_hazmat"],
        prefix="dest_code.str.startswith('MIA')",
        suffix="dest_code.str.endswith('9')",
    )
    assert list(res2["prefix"]) == [False, True, False, False]
    assert list(res2["suffix"]) == [False, True, False, False]


def test_mutate_custom_function_lambda_vectorized_and_map():
    import numpy as np

    def route_shipment(origin: str, dest: str, hazmat_code: str | None) -> str:
        if origin == dest:
            return "Local Courier"
        if "-EXP-" in dest or hazmat_code is not None:
            return "Special Freight"
        return "Standard Ground"

    def calc_metric(x, y):
        return x * 2.5 + np.maximum(y, 0)

    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "origin_hub": ["NYC", "LAX", "ORD", "SEA"],
            "dest_code": ["NYC", "MIA-EXP-9", "DAL", "BOS"],
            "hazmat_class": [None, None, "CLASS-3", None],
            "a": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0],
            "b": [10.0, -5.0, 20.0, -1.0],
        }
    )

    # Row-wise map() and vectorized direct call in the same mutate, plus interleaved string formula
    res = df.mutate(
        shipping_mode=lambda d: map(route_shipment, d["origin_hub"], d["dest_code"], d["hazmat_class"]),
        metric=lambda d: calc_metric(d["a"], d["b"]),
        max_ab=lambda d: np.maximum(d["a"], d["b"]),
        combined="metric + max_ab",
    )
    assert list(res["shipping_mode"]) == ["Local Courier", "Special Freight", "Special Freight", "Standard Ground"]
    assert list(res["metric"]) == [12.5, 5.0, 27.5, 10.0]
    assert list(res["max_ab"]) == [10.0, 2.0, 20.0, 4.0]
    assert list(res["combined"]) == [22.5, 7.0, 47.5, 14.0]


def test_mutate_custom_function_grouped_and_unknown_string_func_raises():
    def scale_with_offset(x, factor=2.0, offset=1.0):
        return x * factor + offset

    def scalar_tag(x, prefix="val"):
        if x > 5:
            return f"{prefix}_high"
        return f"{prefix}_low"

    def group_demeaned(s):
        return s - s.mean()

    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "grp": ["A", "A", "B", "B"],
            "x": [2.0, 8.0, 4.0, 10.0],
        }
    )

    res = df.mutate(
        scaled=lambda d: scale_with_offset(d["x"], 3.0, offset=0.5),
        tag=lambda d: map(lambda v: scalar_tag(v, prefix="item"), d["x"]),
    )
    assert list(res["scaled"]) == [6.5, 24.5, 12.5, 30.5]
    assert list(res["tag"]) == ["item_low", "item_high", "item_low", "item_high"]

    # Grouped execution via .by()
    res_grp = df.by("grp").mutate(demeaned=lambda g: group_demeaned(g["x"]))
    assert list(res_grp["demeaned"]) == [-3.0, 3.0, -3.0, 3.0]

    # Unknown function inside string expression raises ValueError
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Unsupported AST node"):
        df.mutate(bad="scale_with_offset(x)")


def test_mutate_inline_cast_python_types():
    import polars as pl

    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "s_num": ["10", "20", "30"],
            "f_num": [1.9, 2.1, 3.8],
            "i_num": [0, 1, 0],
        }
    )

    # int(x), float(x), str(x), bool(x)
    res = df.mutate(
        i_from_s="int(s_num)",
        i_from_f="int(f_num)",
        f_from_s="float(s_num)",
        s_from_f="str(f_num)",
        b_from_i="bool(i_num)",
    )
    assert res.schema["i_from_s"] == pl.Int64
    assert res.schema["i_from_f"] == pl.Int64
    assert res.schema["f_from_s"] == pl.Float64
    assert res.schema["s_from_f"] == pl.String
    assert res.schema["b_from_i"] == pl.Boolean

    assert res["i_from_s"].to_list() == [10, 20, 30]
    assert res["i_from_f"].to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    assert res["f_from_s"].to_list() == [10.0, 20.0, 30.0]
    assert res["b_from_i"].to_list() == [False, True, False]


def test_mutate_inline_cast_sized_types():
    import polars as pl

    df = pt.DataFrame({"val": ["100", "200"]})
    res = df.mutate(
        i32_cast="int32(val)",
        f32_cast="float32(val)",
        i16_cast="int16(val)",
        u32_cast="uint32(val)",
    )
    assert res.schema["i32_cast"] == pl.Int32
    assert res.schema["f32_cast"] == pl.Float32
    assert res.schema["i16_cast"] == pl.Int16
    assert res.schema["u32_cast"] == pl.UInt32
    assert res["i32_cast"].to_list() == [100, 200]
    assert res["f32_cast"].to_list() == [100.0, 200.0]


def test_mutate_multi_column_cast():
    import polars as pl

    df = pt.DataFrame({"a": ["1", "2"], "b": ["3", "4"]})
    res = df.mutate("(a, b) = int(_)")
    assert res.schema["a"] == pl.Int64
    assert res.schema["b"] == pl.Int64
    assert res["a"].to_list() == [1, 2]
    assert res["b"].to_list() == [3, 4]


def test_mutate_first_last_window():
    # 1. Grouped with by()
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "ticker": ["AAPL", "AAPL", "AAPL", "MSFT", "MSFT"],
            "price": [150.0, 155.0, 160.0, 300.0, 310.0],
        }
    )
    res = df.by("ticker").mutate(
        base="first(price)",
        last_val="last(price)",
        base_method="price.first()",
        last_method="price.last()",
        drift="price - first(price)",
    )
    assert res["base"].to_list() == [150.0, 150.0, 150.0, 300.0, 300.0]
    assert res["last_val"].to_list() == [160.0, 160.0, 160.0, 310.0, 310.0]
    assert res["base_method"].to_list() == [150.0, 150.0, 150.0, 300.0, 300.0]
    assert res["last_method"].to_list() == [160.0, 160.0, 160.0, 310.0, 310.0]
    assert res["drift"].to_list() == [0.0, 5.0, 10.0, 0.0, 10.0]

    # 2. Whole-table (ungrouped)
    res_all = df.mutate(
        first_all="first(price)",
        last_all="last(price)",
    )
    assert res_all["first_all"].to_list() == [150.0, 150.0, 150.0, 150.0, 150.0]
    assert res_all["last_all"].to_list() == [310.0, 310.0, 310.0, 310.0, 310.0]


def test_mutate_direct_polars_expr():
    import polars as pl

    df = pt.DataFrame({"x": [10, 20, 30]})
    res = df.mutate(
        tier=pl.when(pl.col("x") > 25).then(pl.lit("High")).otherwise(pl.lit("Low"))
    )
    assert res["tier"].to_list() == ["Low", "Low", "High"]

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

import pytae as pt
from pytae import cli


@pytest.fixture
def sales_df():
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Region": ["East", "East", "West", "West", "East"],
            "Store": ["S1", "S2", "S1", "S2", "S1"],
            "Year": [2023, 2023, 2023, 2024, 2024],
            "Quarter": ["Q1", "Q2", "Q1", "Q1", "Q2"],
            "Sales": [100.0, 200.0, 300.0, 400.0, 150.0],
            "Profit": [10.0, 25.0, 35.0, 50.0, 20.0],
        }
    )


def test_pivot_both_r_and_c(sales_df):
    res = sales_df.pt.pivot(r="Region", c="Year", v="Sales", a="sum")
    assert isinstance(res, (pt.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame))
    assert list(res.columns) == ["Region", "2023", "2024"]
    assert res.columns.name is None
    assert list(res.index) == [0, 1]

    east_row = res[res["Region"] == "East"].iloc[0]
    assert east_row["2023"] == 300.0  # 100 + 200
    assert east_row["2024"] == 150.0

    west_row = res[res["Region"] == "West"].iloc[0]
    assert west_row["2023"] == 300.0
    assert west_row["2024"] == 400.0


def test_pivot_r_only(sales_df):
    res = pt.pivot(sales_df, r="Region", v="Sales", a="sum")
    assert list(res.columns) == ["Region", "Sales"]
    assert res.columns.name is None
    assert len(res) == 2
    assert res.loc[res["Region"] == "East", "Sales"].iloc[0] == 450.0
    assert res.loc[res["Region"] == "West", "Sales"].iloc[0] == 700.0


def test_pivot_c_only(sales_df):
    res = sales_df.pt.pivot(c="Year", v="Sales", a="sum")
    assert list(res.columns) == ["2023", "2024"]
    assert len(res) == 1
    assert res["2023"].iloc[0] == 600.0
    assert res["2024"].iloc[0] == 550.0


def test_pivot_neither_r_nor_c(sales_df):
    res = sales_df.pt.pivot(v="Sales", a="sum")
    assert list(res.columns) == ["Sales"]
    assert len(res) == 1
    assert res["Sales"].iloc[0] == 1150.0


def test_pivot_multiple_rows(sales_df):
    res = sales_df.pt.pivot(r=["Region", "Store"], c="Year", v="Sales", a="sum")
    assert list(res.columns[:2]) == ["Region", "Store"]
    assert "2023" in res.columns
    assert "2024" in res.columns
    assert len(res) == 4  # East-S1, East-S2, West-S1, West-S2 -> 4 combinations
    assert res.columns.name is None


def test_pivot_multiple_values(sales_df):
    res = sales_df.pt.pivot(r="Region", c="Year", v=["Sales", "Profit"], a="sum")
    assert res.columns[0] == "Region"
    assert "Sales_2023" in res.columns
    assert "Profit_2023" in res.columns
    assert "Sales_2024" in res.columns
    assert "Profit_2024" in res.columns
    assert not isinstance(res.columns, pd.MultiIndex)


def test_pivot_multiple_columns(sales_df):
    res = sales_df.pt.pivot(r="Region", c=["Year", "Quarter"], v="Sales", a="sum")
    assert res.columns[0] == "Region"
    # Column names are flattened with underscore
    assert any("2023_Q1" in col for col in res.columns)
    assert not isinstance(res.columns, pd.MultiIndex)


def test_pivot_agg_n_alias(sales_df):
    res = sales_df.pt.pivot(r="Region", c="Year", v="Sales", a="n")
    assert list(res.columns) == ["Region", "2023", "2024"]
    assert res["2023"].dtype == "int64"
    assert res["2024"].dtype == "int64"
    east_row = res[res["Region"] == "East"].iloc[0]
    assert east_row["2023"] == 2  # two rows for East in 2023
    assert east_row["2024"] == 1


def test_pivot_agg_n_fill_zero_by_default():
    # If a combination has 0 occurrences, it should be 0 and int64
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Island": ["Biscoe", "Biscoe", "Dream"],
            "Species": ["Adelie", "Gentoo", "Chinstrap"],
            "Sex": ["M", "F", "M"],
        }
    )
    res = df.pt.pivot(r="Island", c="Species", v="Sex", a="n")
    assert list(res.columns) == ["Island", "Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"]
    assert res["Adelie"].dtype == "int64"
    assert res["Chinstrap"].dtype == "int64"
    assert res["Gentoo"].dtype == "int64"

    biscoe = res[res["Island"] == "Biscoe"].iloc[0]
    assert biscoe["Adelie"] == 1
    assert biscoe["Chinstrap"] == 0
    assert biscoe["Gentoo"] == 1

    dream = res[res["Island"] == "Dream"].iloc[0]
    assert dream["Adelie"] == 0
    assert dream["Chinstrap"] == 1
    assert dream["Gentoo"] == 0


def test_pivot_agg_n_r_only(sales_df):
    res = sales_df.pt.pivot(r="Region", v="Sales", a="n")
    assert list(res.columns) == ["Region", "Sales"]
    assert res["Sales"].dtype == "int64"
    assert res.loc[res["Region"] == "East", "Sales"].iloc[0] == 3
    assert res.loc[res["Region"] == "West", "Sales"].iloc[0] == 2


def test_pivot_agg_n_c_only(sales_df):
    res = sales_df.pt.pivot(c="Year", v="Sales", a="n")
    assert list(res.columns) == ["2023", "2024"]
    assert res["2023"].dtype == "int64"
    assert res["2024"].dtype == "int64"
    assert res["2023"].iloc[0] == 3
    assert res["2024"].iloc[0] == 2


def test_pivot_agg_n_neither_r_nor_c(sales_df):
    res = sales_df.pt.pivot(v="Sales", a="n")
    assert list(res.columns) == ["Sales"]
    assert res["Sales"].dtype == "int64"
    assert res["Sales"].iloc[0] == 5


def test_pivot_agg_n_explicit_nan_fill():
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Island": ["Biscoe", "Dream"],
            "Species": ["Adelie", "Chinstrap"],
            "Sex": ["M", "F"],
        }
    )
    res = df.pt.pivot(r="Island", c="Species", v="Sex", a="n", f_v=np.nan)
    # When explicit NaN fill is requested, missing combinations are <NA> of Int64 dtype
    assert res["Adelie"].dtype == "Int64"
    assert res["Chinstrap"].dtype == "Int64"
    assert pd.isna(res.loc[res["Island"] == "Dream", "Adelie"].iloc[0])
    assert res.loc[res["Island"] == "Dream", "Chinstrap"].iloc[0] == 1


def test_pivot_f_v_explicit(sales_df):
    res = sales_df.pt.pivot(r=["Region", "Store"], c="Year", v="Sales", a="sum", f_v=0.0)
    # Check that missing combinations have 0.0 instead of NaN
    assert not res.isna().any().any()


def test_pivot_dropna_false_default():
    df_na = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Region": ["East", np.nan, "West"],
            "Year": [2023, 2023, np.nan],
            "Sales": [10.0, 20.0, 30.0],
        }
    )
    res = df_na.pt.pivot(r="Region", c="Year", v="Sales", a="sum")
    # Region has NaN, so there should be a row with NaN in Region
    assert res["Region"].isna().any()
    # Year has NaN, so there should be a column representing nan
    col_names = [str(c) for c in res.columns]
    assert any("nan" in c.lower() for c in col_names)


def test_pivot_aliases_rejected(sales_df):
    for bad_kw in (
        {"rows": "Region"},
        {"cols": "Year"},
        {"values": "Sales"},
        {"aggfunc": "mean"},
        {"index": "Region"},
        {"columns": "Year"},
        {"fill": 0.0},
        {"fill_value": 0.0},
    ):
        with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="pivot\\(\\) got unexpected keyword argument\\(s\\)"):
            sales_df.pt.pivot(r="Region", c="Year", v="Sales", **bad_kw)


def test_pivot_optional_v(sales_df):
    # 2D cross-tabulation count matrix with v omitted
    res = sales_df.pt.pivot(r="Region", c="Year")
    assert list(res.columns) == ["Region", "2023", "2024"]
    assert res.loc[res["Region"] == "East", "2023"].iloc[0] == 2
    assert res.loc[res["Region"] == "East", "2024"].iloc[0] == 1
    assert res.loc[res["Region"] == "West", "2023"].iloc[0] == 1
    assert res.loc[res["Region"] == "West", "2024"].iloc[0] == 1

    # 1D row frequency table with v omitted
    res_1d = sales_df.pt.pivot(r="Region,Store")
    assert list(res_1d.columns) == ["Region", "Store", "n"]
    assert len(res_1d) == 4
    assert res_1d["n"].sum() == 5

    # 1D column frequency table with v omitted
    res_col = sales_df.pt.pivot(c="Year")
    assert list(res_col.columns) == ["2023", "2024"]
    assert res_col["2023"].iloc[0] == 3
    assert res_col["2024"].iloc[0] == 2

    # 0D total count with v omitted
    res_0d = sales_df.pt.pivot()
    assert list(res_0d.columns) == ["n"]
    assert res_0d["n"].iloc[0] == 5

    # v omitted but incompatible agg function requested
    with pytest.raises(
        ValueError,
        match="pivot\\(\\): value column 'v' is required when aggregation function is 'mean'. Omit 'v' for row counts.",
    ):
        sales_df.pt.pivot(r="Region", c="Year", a="mean")

    with pytest.raises(
        ValueError,
        match="pivot\\(\\): value column 'v' is required when aggregation function is 'median'. Omit 'v' for row counts.",
    ):
        sales_df.pt.pivot(r="Region", c="Year", a="median")


def test_pivot_f_v(sales_df):
    res = sales_df.pt.pivot(r="Region", c="Quarter", v="Sales", a="sum", f_v=0)
    assert not res.isna().any().any()
    assert (res["Q1"] >= 0).all()


def test_pivot_unknown_column_error(sales_df):
    with pytest.raises(KeyError, match="not found in DataFrame"):
        sales_df.pt.pivot(r="NonExistent", c="Year", v="Sales")


def test_wide_r_spec(sales_df):
    tall = sales_df.pt.long(cols=["Sales", "Profit"], id_vars=["Region", "Store", "Year"])
    back = tall.pt.wide(r=["Region", "Store", "Year"], c="variable", v="value")
    assert "Sales" in back.columns
    assert "Profit" in back.columns

def test_cli_pivot_basic(tmp_path, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Region": ["East", "East", "West"],
            "Year": [2023, 2024, 2023],
            "Sales": [100, 150, 200],
        }
    )
    path = str(tmp_path / "data.csv")
    df.to_csv(path, index=False)

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-pivot", "r=Region,c=Year,v=Sales,a=sum"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "East" in captured.out
    assert "West" in captured.out
    assert "2023" in captured.out
    assert "2024" in captured.out

def test_cli_pivot_export_parquet(tmp_path):
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Region": ["East", "West"],
            "Year": [2023, 2024],
            "Sales": [100, 200],
        }
    )
    in_path = str(tmp_path / "in.csv")
    out_path = str(tmp_path / "out.parquet")
    df.to_csv(in_path, index=False)

    exit_code = cli.main([in_path, "-pivot", "r=Region,c=Year,v=Sales", "-o", out_path])
    assert exit_code == 0

    assert "Region" in pivoted_df.columns
    assert "2023" in pivoted_df.columns
    assert "2024" in pivoted_df.columns


def test_pivot_no_cartesian_product_unobserved_combinations():
    doc = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Region": ["East", "East", "East", "East", "West", "West"],
            "Store": ["Store A", "Store A", "Store B", "Store B", "Store C", "Store C"],
            "Year": [2023, 2024, 2023, 2024, 2023, 2024],
            "Sales": [700.0, 850.0, 800.0, 950.0, 900.0, 1100.0],
        }
    )
    res_sum = doc.pt.pivot(r=["Region", "Store"], c="Year", v="Sales", a="sum")
    # Only observed Region-Store pairs should exist (3 rows), not 6
    assert len(res_sum) == 3
    assert set(res_sum["Store"]) == {"Store A", "Store B", "Store C"}

    res_n = doc.pt.pivot(r=["Region", "Store"], c="Year", v="Sales", a="n")
    assert len(res_n) == 3


def test_pivot_multi_c_cols_a_n_preserves_outer_keys():
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Region": ["East", "East", "East", "East"],
            "Year": [2023, 2023, 2023, 2024],
            "Quarter": ["Q1", "Q1", "Q2", "Q1"],
            "Sales": [1, 1, 1, 1],
        }
    )
    out = df.pt.pivot(r="Region", c=["Year", "Quarter"], v="Sales", a="n")
    assert "2023_Q1" in out.columns
    assert "2023_Q2" in out.columns
    assert "2024_Q1" in out.columns
    assert out["2023_Q1"].iloc[0] == 2
    assert out["2023_Q2"].iloc[0] == 1
    assert out["2024_Q1"].iloc[0] == 1


def test_pivot_header_deduplication():
    df1 = pd.DataFrame({"r": ["a", "a"], "c": [1, "1"], "v": [10.0, 20.0]})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="contain duplicate names"):
        df1.pt.pivot(r="r", c="c", v="v", a="sum")

    df2 = pd.DataFrame({"r": ["a", "a", "a"], "c": [np.nan, "nan", "ok"], "v": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="contain duplicate names"):
        df2.pt.pivot(r="r", c="c", v="v", a="sum")


def test_pivot_c_only_multi_values_keeps_metric_index():
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Year": [2023, 2024, 2023],
            "Sales": [100.0, 150.0, 200.0],
            "Profit": [10.0, 15.0, 20.0],
        }
    )
    out = df.pt.pivot(c="Year", v=["Sales", "Profit"], a="sum")
    assert "metric" in out.columns
    assert set(out["metric"]) == {"Sales", "Profit"}


def test_pivot_row_only_a_n_count_key_collision():
    df1 = pd.DataFrame({"island": ["A", "A", "B"]})
    out1 = df1.pt.pivot(r="island", a="n")
    assert "island" in out1.columns
    assert "n" in out1.columns
    assert list(out1["n"]) == [2, 1]

    # If v is specified and overlaps with r, raise ValueError
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="cannot also be in grouping dimensions"):
        df1.pt.pivot(r="island", v="island", a="n")

    # If row grouping column is named "n", omitting v will default to "n" which collides
    df_colliding = pd.DataFrame({"n": ["a", "a", "b"], "val": [1, 2, 3]})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="collides with row grouping column"):
        df_colliding.pt.pivot(r="n", a="n")

    # Providing a non-colliding column for v works
    out_custom = df_colliding.pt.pivot(r="n", v="val", a="n")
    assert list(out_custom.columns) == ["n", "val"]


def test_pivot_v_in_dimensions_validation():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"Region": ["East", "West"], "Year": [2023, 2024], "Sales": [10, 20]})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="cannot also be in grouping dimensions"):
        df.pt.pivot(r="Region", c="Year", v="Region", a="sum")
